sources.platform: arXiv / Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research
sources.notes: Kotseruba & Tsotsos (2018). A Review of 40 Years of Cognitive Architecture Research. arXiv:1610.08602 (also in JAIR). Surveys 84 cognitive architectures and 900+ projects across 40 years. Analyzes core abilities: perception, attention, action selection, memory, learning, reasoning, meta-cognition. Gold-standard survey for cognitive AI design. WALCHE relevance: validates multi-component healing/meta-engine design pattern; provides taxonomy of memory and learning mechanisms that map directly to WALCHE corpus KB layers and VLL. Download: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1610.08602

Langley (2009). Cognitive Architectures: Research Issues and Challenges. Cognitive Systems Research. Foundational paper defining core research challenges in cognitive architecture: unified cognition, learning, knowledge representation, reactive/deliberative balance. Complements Kotseruba survey. WALCHE relevance: identifies same tension between reactive healing (HealingEngine) and deliberative planning (MetaEngine/council) that WALCHE resolves via dual-mode architecture.

sources.notes: Laird (2012). The Soar Cognitive Architecture. MIT Press. Definitive reference for the Soar unified theory of cognition — one of the longest-running and most influential cognitive architectures (1983–present). Covers: production memory, working memory, long-term memory (procedural/semantic/episodic), chunking (learning), reinforcement learning, perception, action. WALCHE relevance: Soar's production-rule + chunking model maps to WALCHE's RubricScorer + VLL weight-update mechanism. WALCHE MetaEngine's loop registry parallels Soar's universal subgoaling. Soar also has explicit episodic memory (epmem) and semantic memory (smem) — direct design precedent for WALCHE KB tiers.

Laird et al. (2017). A Standard Model of the Mind: Toward a Common Computational Framework across Artificial Intelligence, Cognitive Science, Neuroscience, and Robotics. AI Magazine 38(4). Defines the Common Model of Cognition (CMC) — consensus architecture across Soar, ACT-R, Sigma, and other major architectures. CMC specifies: working memory (attention/perception), long-term memory (procedural/declarative/episodic), action selection, learning, meta-cognition. WALCHE relevance: CMC provides the theoretical framework to formally validate WALCHE's architecture. WALCHE's components (MetaEngine, HealingEngine, RubricScorer, VLL, ProvenanceLog) map onto CMC memory + learning + meta-cognitive slots. Download via AAAI digital library or authors' websites.

sources.notes: TsinghuaC3I/Awesome-Memory-for-Agents (GitHub). Curated list of LLM/agent memory papers with taxonomy: Short-Term Memory, Long-Term Memory (Episodic/Experiential), Personalization, Self-Evolution. Includes MemGPT, Reflexion, and many others. README is a structured markdown corpus source — extremely high density for AI memory design. Also add to Queue 4C: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/TsinghuaC3I/Awesome-Memory-for-Agents. WALCHE relevance: taxonomy maps directly to WALCHE KB tiers (STM=working context, LTM=walche_kb.json, episodic=provenance.jsonl). Self-evolution category maps directly to VLL.

Packer et al. (2023). MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems. arXiv:2310.08560. Introduces tiered memory hierarchy for LLMs: in-context (main context window = fast), external storage (disk = slow), and virtual context management via OS-inspired paging. Enables unlimited-length conversations and document analysis via intelligent context eviction/retrieval. WALCHE relevance: MemGPT's memory tiers (in-context vs external KB) map exactly to WALCHE's corpus.integrity architecture — walche_kb.json is WALCHE's 'external disk', working context is 'main memory'. MemGPT's context management strategy validates WALCHE's PreIngestGate + corpus scoring design. Download: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2310.08560

Shinn et al. (2023). Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning. arXiv:2303.11366. NeurIPS 2023. Agents improve via self-reflection: on task failure, agent verbally critiques its trajectory and stores the critique in episodic memory, then retries. Uses linguistic feedback (vs gradient updates) as the learning signal. WALCHE relevance: Reflexion IS the VLL (Verification Learning Loop) mechanism described in WALCHE terminology. WALCHE's VLL proposal generation + SOVEREIGN_REVIEW pattern = Reflexion's verbal reflection + episodic memory storage. VLL Cross Gate (rubric_ok/risk_ok) = Reflexion's success evaluator. This paper gives the academic foundation for WALCHE's VLL — once corpus.integrity > 0.85, VLL proposals will be accepted the same way Reflexion's reflections are. Download: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2303.11366

Garcez & Lamb (2023). Neurosymbolic AI: The 3rd Wave. arXiv:2012.05876. Foundational NeSy position paper — argues that the 3rd wave of AI requires integration of robust neural learning with symbolic knowledge representation, reasoning, and explainability. Defines NeSy as hybrid systems combining connectionist (neural) and symbolic (logic/rules/KR) components. Establishes the theoretical basis for why pure deep learning fails on interpretability, robustness, and systematic generalization. WALCHE relevance: WALCHE's entire architecture IS a NeSy system — neural corpus ingestion + symbolic guardrails, rubric scoring, FMEA, and VLL policy rules. This paper gives the 3rd-wave theoretical foundation for WALCHE's hybrid design. Download: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2012.05876

Kautz (2022). The Third AI Summer. AI Magazine 43(1):93-104. AAAI Robert S. Engelmore Memorial Award Lecture. Defines the canonical 6-type taxonomy of neural-symbolic coupling (loose to tight): (1) Symbol_x_Neural — isolated, no coupling; (2) Neural|Symbol — sequential pipeline; (3) Neural:Symbol — neural embedded inside symbolic; (4) Neural~Symbol — compiled/distilled; (5) Neural[Symbol] — symbolic embedded inside neural; (6) Fully integrated bidirectional. WALCHE architecture classification: WALCHE is primarily Type 2-3 (Neural|Symbol sequential: neural corpus ingestion feeds symbolic FMEA/Rubric scoring; VLL is Type 3: symbolic policy rules derived from neural outputs embedded within neural pipeline). Full paper: https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/aimagazine/article/view/19122

Colelough (2024). Neuro-Symbolic AI in 2024: A Systematic Review. Covers 2020-2024 NeSy landscape. Taxonomy: knowledge representation (KR), learning/inference integration, interpretability, robustness. Most current survey — captures post-LLM NeSy developments including LLM+symbolic hybrid systems. WALCHE relevance: 2024 taxonomy will include LLM-grounded symbolic systems most similar to WALCHE's design (LLM-driven healing proposals + symbolic rubric/guardrail verification). Search: Google Scholar 'Neuro-Symbolic AI 2024 Systematic Review Colelough' or arXiv.

Nawaz et al. (2025). A review of neuro-symbolic AI integrating reasoning and learning. Techniques for cognitive systems. Most recent (2025) — covers integration of neural learning with symbolic reasoning specifically for cognitive AI systems. Directly relevant to WALCHE as a cognitive looping system. WALCHE's PAIN-FMEA + healing loop is a cognitive NeSy reasoning engine. Search arXiv 2025 for 'neuro-symbolic reasoning learning cognitive systems Nawaz'.

Lu et al. (2024). Surveying neuro-symbolic approaches for reliable AI. IoT/reliability focus. Categories: knowledge graphs (KG), semantic parsing, logical reasoning, VQA, agents/planning. Reliability + IoT angle is directly relevant to WALCHE's self-healing reliability goal. WALCHE functions as a reliability-focused NeSy system: neural corpus intake + symbolic failure detection (PAIN-FMEA) + symbolic recovery planning (HealingEngine proposals). Search arXiv 2024 for 'neuro-symbolic reliable AI IoT survey Lu'.

GitHub: scallop-lang/scallop. WALCHE use: LTN semantic constraints could formalize GuardRail rules as differentiable FOL constraints on corpus item property tensors. (3) NLM (Neural Logic Machines, Evans & Grefenstette) — neural networks that execute over logical predicates with inductive learning. WALCHE use: NLM could handle PAIN-FMEA's predicate-based failure mode reasoning. Also: LLM-SS (LLM + symbolic solver hybrid) patterns for VLL policy generation. Zia et al. (2023). Topological Deep Learning: A Review of an Emerging Paradigm. arXiv:2302.03836. Core TDL survey: TDA concepts (persistent homology, Betti numbers, filtration), integration into DL frameworks (topological layers, topological analytics), simplicial/cell complex architectures, challenges and future directions. WALCHE relevance: TDL's persistent homology provides a mathematically rigorous way to analyze corpus item relationships and multi-scale structure — potential upgrade path for WALCHE's CEVIP Cross-Ensemble phase to detect topological anomalies in corpus content graphs. Hensel et al. (2021). A Survey of Topological Machine Learning Methods. Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence. TDA + ML symbiosis: persistent homology as features for classical ML, enhancement of deep learning models with topological invariants, topological regularization. Open access — available at Frontiers website. DOI: 10.3389/frai.2021.681108. Search 'Hensel topological machine learning survey Frontiers 2021' for direct download link.

Position paper arguing TDL superiority for higher-order/relational data via simplicial and combinatorial complexes (vs standard GNNs limited to pairwise edges). WALCHE application: CEVIP corpus graph has higher-order relationships (document clusters, semantic chains, cross-genre links) — TDL topological layers could model n-way document relationships that pairwise embedding similarity misses. Masood (2026). Loop Engineering: A Guide for Engineers and Practitioners. Medium. Covers: loop design principles, verification strategies, governance, failure mode taxonomy (infinite loops, error amplification, divergence, confirmation bias in reflection loops), cost control, observability instrumentation. HIGH PRIORITY for WALCHE — this is the exact engineering discipline WALCHE implements. WALCHE's 4-cycle forensic healing loop, PAIN-FMEA failure mode registry, and C12 judgment gate map directly onto the loop governance and failure mode sections. Save page as .md via browser Markdown extension. Search Medium for 'Loop Engineering Guide Engineers Practitioners Masood 2026'.

LangChain (2026). The Art of Loop Engineering. LangChain official blog. Covers: stacking agent loops (inner reasoning loop + outer verification loop), event-driven loops (reactive to environment signals), memory loops (context accumulation across iterations), instrumentation strategies for loop reliability (tracing, timeout guards, step counters). WALCHE architecture parallel: WALCHE stacks exactly these loop types — MetaEngine (event-driven), HealingEngine (verification loop), VLL (memory loop via corpus KB updates), GuardRail (loop governor). Save from blog.langchain.com. Search 'The Art of Loop Engineering LangChain 2026'.

Oracle (2026). What Is the AI Agent Loop? Oracle blog/docs. Covers: core iterative cycle (Perception → Reason → Act → Observe), ReAct pattern comparisons across major frameworks (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK). Enterprise framing — reliability, governance, enterprise agent deployment. WALCHE parallel: WALCHE's run_system.py implements this exact perception-reason-act-observe cycle via the inject→dream→heal→test→audit phase pipeline. Oracle's framework comparison table is useful for positioning WALCHE vs LangGraph/AutoGen in the ecosystem. Save from oracle.com/artificial-intelligence/. Search 'What Is the AI Agent Loop Oracle 2026'.

Mem0 (2026). Loop Engineering for AI Agents: Memory-First Design. Mem0 blog. Covers: persistent memory integrated into control loops for agent autonomy, memory-first loop architecture (loop state stored in persistent KB, not ephemeral context), reducing manual intervention via memory-informed loop termination decisions. WALCHE parallel: WALCHE's corpus KB (walche_kb.json) is exactly a persistent memory layer for the healing loop — lessons_learned.jsonl records loop outcomes that inform future loop iterations. Mem0's memory-first design validates WALCHE's architecture. Save from mem0.ai/blog. Search 'Loop Engineering Memory-First Design Mem0 2026'.

MindStudio (2026). What Is Loop Engineering? MindStudio blog. Covers: /loop, /goal, /routines abstractions for continuous self-directed workflows; ReAct foundations as the substrate for loop engineering; structured loop types: goal-directed (terminate on task completion), routine-driven (periodic execution), event-driven (trigger on signal). WALCHE parallel: WALCHE's --phase full argument maps to a goal-directed loop; --phase heal maps to a routine-driven loop with 4-cycle termination. MindStudio's /goal termination abstraction is a clean model for WALCHE's C12 judgment gate. Save from mindstudio.ai/blog. Search 'What Is Loop Engineering MindStudio 2026'.

Yao et al. (2022). ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models. arXiv:2210.03629. The foundational paper for reason+act looping in LLMs: interleaves chain-of-thought reasoning traces with task-specific actions (search, lookup, API calls). Benchmark results on HotpotQA, Fever, ALFWorld, WebShop demonstrate that reason+act looping outperforms pure reasoning (CoT) or pure acting. WALCHE is a ReAct-class system: the healing loop's Diagnosis→Proposal→Apply→Verify cycle is structurally identical to ReAct's Thought→Action→Observation cycle. This paper is the academic grounding for WALCHE's core loop design. Pair with Reflexion (batch 20, already logged as reflexion_shinn_2023) for the self-improvement extension. Download: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2210.03629

Four loop engineering implementation frameworks: (1) LangGraph (langchain-ai/langgraph) — stateful loop graphs for agents; explicit cycle/loop nodes with conditional edges; built-in state persistence and human-in-the-loop checkpointing. Most directly comparable to WALCHE's run_system.py phase graph. Clone: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph. (2) AutoGen (microsoft/autogen) — multi-agent conversation loops with termination conditions; GroupChat loop orchestration. (3) CrewAI (crewAIInc/crewAI) — role-based agent loop orchestration with task delegation. (4) OpenAI Agents SDK (openai/openai-agents-python) — official SDK for OpenAI agent loops with function-calling and tool-use integration. KEY WALCHE FINDING: LangGraph's conditional edge pattern (state → condition_check → continue|terminate) is a production-ready model for replacing WALCHE's current C12 judgment gate with a more robust graph-based termination decision. RISK NOTE: all four frameworks contain the risks documented in this batch — infinite loop guard patterns in each framework's source code are high-value corpus content.

Dafny — verification-aware programming language with built-in contracts (preconditions, postconditions, loop invariants, termination proofs) backed by Z3 SMT solver. Used by Amazon (AWS services), Intel, and Microsoft for provably-correct code. Key Leino papers: 'Dafny: An Automatic Program Verifier for Functional Correctness' (LPAR 2010); 'Program Proofs' book (Leino, MIT Press 2023). Clone: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/dafny-lang/dafny. WALCHE application: Dafny contracts could formally specify WALCHE's loop invariants (corpus.integrity must monotonically improve across cycles), HealingEngine postconditions (proposal.applied=true ↔ rubric_score improved), and GuardRail preconditions (risk_score < threshold → apply). This is the most direct formal verification path for WALCHE bug-free guarantees.

TLA+ (Temporal Logic of Actions) — Leslie Lamport's specification language for modeling and verifying concurrent and distributed systems. TLC model checker exhaustively verifies safety and liveness properties over all reachable states. Used by AWS (14+ distributed system specs), Microsoft Azure. Key resources: Lamport's 'Specifying Systems' book (free PDF at lamport.azurewebsites.net), TLA+ community modules (github.com/tlaplus/CommunityModules), TLA+ Examples (github.com/tlaplus/Examples). Clone toolbox: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/tlaplus/tlaplus. WALCHE application: TLA+ can model WALCHE's 4-cycle forensic healing loop as a concurrent state machine — verifying that the loop always terminates (liveness), never corrupts corpus state (safety), and that C12 judgment gate correctly gatekeeps proposal application. Critical for detecting subtle race conditions if WALCHE ever runs parallel heal cycles.

Three interactive theorem provers for verified mathematics and code: (1) Lean 4 (leanprover/lean4, https://leanprover.github.io/) — dependent type theory; Mathlib4 is the world's largest machine-verified math library (~100k theorems). Increasingly used for AI-verified reasoning: WALCHE's RubricScorer could be replaced with a Lean-verified scoring function with formal correctness proofs. Clone: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/leanprover/lean4; also clone Mathlib4: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4. (2) Coq / Rocq (coq-community/coq, https://coq.inria.fr/) — dependent types with extraction to OCaml/Haskell; CompCert (verified C compiler) built in Coq. Clone: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/coq/coq. (3) Isabelle/HOL (https://isabelle.in.tum.de/) — higher-order logic with powerful automation; used for seL4 microkernel proof (8 MLOC verified OS). Isabelle download is .tar.gz from official site (not GitHub). WALCHE application: Lean 4 + Mathlib is the most accessible for verifying WALCHE's mathematical scoring functions; Coq for extracting verified OCaml implementations of critical CEVIP phases.

awesome-formal-verification (GitHub curated list) — comprehensive index of formal verification tools, theorem provers, model checkers, SMT solvers, verification languages, tutorials, and verified software projects. Multiple repos exist: search GitHub for 'awesome-formal-verification'. High corpus density per KB size — structured markdown with tool classifications, maturity levels, and use case descriptions. Clone whichever is most recently maintained. Complements Dafny, TLA+, Lean 4, Coq/Isabelle entries as a navigation map of the full formal verification landscape.

From Natural Language to Verified Code (2026). LLM + Dafny pipeline for AI-generated verified code. arXiv:2604.22601. NOTE: verify arXiv ID at arxiv.org before download — ID format 2604.22601 corresponds to April 2026; confirm paper title matches. Pipeline: (1) LLM generates Dafny code with contracts from natural language spec, (2) Dafny verifier checks correctness via Z3, (3) iterative refinement loop until verification passes. This is the most directly applicable paper to WALCHE's build: WALCHE code is currently unverified Python — this pipeline would allow generating Dafny contracts from WALCHE's existing docstrings + PAIN-FMEA failure specs, then verifying the resulting code. HIGHEST PRIORITY formal verification paper for WALCHE. Download: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.22601 (verify ID first).

Four neurotech and cognitive enhancement review sources: (1) AI for neurofunctionalities, Alzheimer's, mental health — PMC systematic reviews and ML/DL application surveys 2024-2025. Search PubMed: 'artificial intelligence cognitive enhancement review 2024' AND 'machine learning Alzheimer detection 2024'. Download open-access PDFs from PMC (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov). (2) AI-powered brain enhancement review 2025 — ricopediatrics.com; covers: neurofeedback + AI, BCI (brain-computer interface) cognitive optimization, AI-driven cognitive training protocols. Search ricopediatrics.com for 'AI brain enhancement cognitive optimization 2025'. (3) Brain Capital initiatives + precision AI nutrition — Baker Institute for Public Policy (bakerinstitute.org) reports on Brain Capital framework and AI-precision nutrition for mental/cognitive health. Search bakerinstitute.org for 'Brain Capital AI'. (4) Explainable AI in closed-loop neurotechnologies — Springer 2026 scoping review. Search SpringerLink or Google Scholar: 'explainable AI closed-loop neurotechnology scoping review 2026'. WALCHE relevance: cognitive enhancement literature validates the human-in-the-loop design of WALCHE's C12 judgment gate — human cognitive augmentation + AI loop = hybrid intelligence system. Brain Capital framework provides an ROI model for WALCHE's corpus investment.

Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) with safeguards — risk/benefit literature for bounded self-improving AI systems. Key papers to acquire: (1) Schmidhuber — Formal theory of creativity, fun, and intrinsic motivation (2010) — mathematical RSI foundations. (2) Yampolskiy (2020) — 'Unpredictability of AI: On the Impossibility of Accurately Predicting All Actions of a Higher Intelligence' — capability explosion risk. (3) Omohundro (2008) — 'The Basic AI Drives' (Singularity Summit) — convergent instrumental goals in RSI. (4) Any 2024-2025 alignment papers on bounded RSI via verifiable specifications. CRITICAL WALCHE RISK NOTE: WALCHE's VLL (Verification Learning Loop) is a bounded RSI mechanism — proposals modify corpus weights, improving future reasoning quality. The loop is currently bounded by: 4-cycle limit, C12 judgment gate, GuardRail risk check. These three safeguards map exactly onto recommended RSI safety mechanisms in the literature. This material should be indexed as WALCHE safety architecture validation AND as training material for WALCHE's GuardRail. Search arXiv: 'recursive self-improvement safety bounds verification 2024'.

Bio-inspired and neuromorphic computing for efficient cognition — low-power, brain-like intelligence substrates. Key reviews: (1) Schuman et al. (2022) — 'Opportunities for Neuromorphic Computing Algorithms and Applications' (Nature Computational Science). (2) Davies et al. (2018) — 'Loihi: A neuromorphic manycore processor with on-chip learning' (Intel Loihi chip). (3) Mahowald & Douglas (1991) — silicon neuron (foundational). (4) Spiking Neural Networks (SNN) survey: Pfeiffer & Pfeil (2018) or Tavanaei et al. (2019) arXiv:1804.08150. WALCHE relevance: neuromorphic principles — event-driven processing, sparse activation, in-memory computation — could inform future WALCHE hardware architecture for local/edge deployment. Lower priority than formal verification but relevant for long-term platform efficiency goals. Search arXiv: 'neuromorphic computing survey 2022 2023 efficient brain-inspired'.

Four model checking and SMT solver tools: (1) Z3 SMT solver (microsoft/z3) — the backbone solver behind Dafny and many formal tools. Python API: `from z3 import *`. Direct use: encode WALCHE's loop invariants as SMT formulas and verify with Z3 directly, without full Dafny. Clone: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Z3Prover/z3. (2) Quint (informalsystems/quint) — modern TLA+-inspired spec language with VS Code integration; more accessible than TLA+. Clone: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/informalsystems/quint. (3) SPIN model checker (nimble/spin or spinroot.com) — Promela language for concurrent system verification; finite state machine exhaustive checking. Classic tool for protocol verification. (4) Alloy Analyzer (AlloyTools/org.alloytools.alloy) — relational/first-order logic for structural specifications; Kodkod SAT backend. Property-based testing tools: Hypothesis (HypothesisWorks/hypothesis) for Python — generates adversarial test cases from property specifications; integrates with pytest. WALCHE application: Z3 Python API is the lowest-friction entry point — can add Z3 invariant checks directly into WALCHE's existing Python code as assertion probes during loop execution. Hypothesis can auto-generate edge-case corpus items to stress-test CEVIP PreIngestGate.

Verified agent loop patterns — combining LangGraph stateful loops with formal specifications for provably-correct agent orchestration. Key pattern: (1) Define loop invariants as TLA+ or Dafny contracts (e.g., token budget monotonically decreases, state machine transitions are acyclic unless explicit cycle is intended). (2) Use property-based testing (Hypothesis) to stress-test the loop with adversarial inputs before formal verification. (3) Add Z3 runtime assertions as lightweight verification probes in production loops. Key sources to acquire: arXiv papers on 'verified LLM agents' or 'formal specification agent loops 2024 2025'; LangGraph docs on state machine patterns (already in Queue 4I as part of langgraph clone); any blog posts on 'LangGraph + TLA+ specification'. WALCHE application: this directly upgrades WALCHE's healing loop from empirically-tested to formally-specified. The four-cycle limit, C12 gate, and GuardRail risk check should each have a formal spec. This is the integration layer connecting NeSy (batch 21), Loop Engineering (batch 24), and Formal Verification (this batch) into a unified verified intelligent loop.

Guo et al. (2022). A Survey on Automated Fact-Checking. Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics (TACL) 10, 178-206. Core AFC pipeline: (1) claim detection — identifying check-worthy claims, (2) evidence retrieval — document/knowledge retrieval for claim context, (3) claim verification — verdict prediction (supported/refuted/insufficient evidence), (4) justification generation — explainable verdicts. Covers: rule-based vs neural verifiers, knowledge-graph grounded verification, dataset benchmarks (FEVER, MultiFC, LIAR). ACL Anthology: aclanthology.org/2022.tacl-1.11. arXiv preprint: search 'Guo survey automated fact-checking 2022 TACL'. WALCHE application: WALCHE's CEVIP pipeline already implements a subset of this AFC architecture — PreIngestGate = claim detection phase, GuardRail = verification gate, CrossEnsemble = evidence retrieval and multi-judge verdict. This paper provides the formal AFC taxonomy to upgrade each CEVIP phase to state-of-the-art specifications.

Multimodal Automated Fact-Checking survey (EMNLP 2023 Findings). Extends AFC to multimodal claims: text + image + video + audio evidence. Covers: cross-modal evidence alignment, multimodal fusion for verdict prediction, dataset benchmarks (NewsCLIPpings, FakeSV, Mocheg). WALCHE application: WALCHE's corpus ingests multimodal content (PDFs with figures, OpenStax textbooks with diagrams). Multimodal AFC techniques can upgrade CEVIP's CrossEnsemble phase to verify cross-modal consistency (e.g., figure captions matching diagram content). Search ACL Anthology EMNLP 2023 Findings for 'multimodal automated fact-checking survey'. Also pairs with VeriTaS benchmark (batch 26 below) for leakage-resistant multimodal verification.

sources.notes: Cartus/Automated-Fact-Checking-Resources (GitHub) — comprehensive curated index of: AFC papers (claim detection, evidence retrieval, verification, explanation), LLM factuality papers, misinfo/disinfo detection methods, adversarial attack papers targeting fact-checkers, AFC datasets and benchmarks. NOTE: verify repo is still actively maintained; if archived, also search for 'awesome-fact-checking' alternatives. WALCHE application: this is the primary navigation map for upgrading CEVIP's verification quality — use to prioritize which AFC papers to acquire next for corpus.

VeriTaS benchmark (2026). Dynamic multimodal AFC benchmark designed for robust, leakage-resistant verification engines. arXiv 2026 — exact arXiv ID not yet confirmed; search arxiv.org for 'VeriTaS multimodal fact-checking benchmark 2026' or 'dynamic automated fact-checking leakage-resistant 2026'. Key innovation: dynamic benchmark construction prevents training data leakage (test claims are generated post-training, preventing benchmark contamination). Robustness testing: verifiers are adversarially stress-tested against claim reformulations, evidence truncation, and multimodal distractors. WALCHE application: VeriTaS's leakage-resistant construction methodology directly maps to WALCHE's CEVIP pipeline — CEVIP's PreIngestGate should reject corpus items that were used in any prior rubric scoring run (prevents feedback loops that inflate corpus.integrity scores artificially). The adversarial stress-testing protocol can be adapted as a WALCHE GuardRail validation suite.

Data poisoning defense surveys — robust ML validation, sanitization, and adversarial training against training/inference pipeline poisons. Key papers to acquire: (1) Goldblum et al. (2023) 'Dataset Security for Machine Learning: Data Poisoning, Backdoor Attacks, and Defenses' (TPAMI) — comprehensive survey; arXiv:2012.10544. (2) Huang et al. (2022) 'Backdoor Defense via Deconfounded Representation Learning' (CVPR) — deconfounded cleaning of poisoned datasets. (3) Chen et al. (2019) 'Detecting Backdoor Attacks on Deep Neural Networks by Activation Clustering' (arXiv:1811.03728) — activation-based poison detection. (4) Any 2024-2025 RAG poisoning defenses (search 'RAG data poisoning defense 2024' — critical for WALCHE corpus KB). (5) 'PoisonedRAG' (arXiv:2402.07867, 2024) — first paper specifically on RAG knowledge base poisoning and defenses. WALCHE application: WALCHE's PreIngestGate is the primary poison defense layer — items with anomalous embeddings, mismatched provenance, or suspiciously high rubric scores on first pass should be quarantined. PoisonedRAG defenses are the most critical to implement — WALCHE's corpus KB is a RAG-style knowledge base.

Sleeper agents and deceptive alignment detection/mitigation papers. Priority papers: (1) Hubinger et al. (2024) 'Sleeper Agents: Training Deceptive LLMs that Persist Through Safety Training' (Anthropic, arXiv:2401.05566) — shows that backdoored behavior can survive RLHF, SFT, and adversarial training; current safety training methods are insufficient against deceptive alignment. Download: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2401.05566. (2) Hubinger et al. (2019) 'Risks from Learned Optimization in Advanced Machine Learning Systems' (arXiv:1906.01820) — mesa-optimization and inner alignment; foundational deceptive alignment theory. (3) Evans et al. (2021) 'Truthful AI: Developing and governing AI that does not lie' (arXiv:2110.06674) — architectures for truth-seeking AI. WALCHE application: WALCHE is vulnerable to deceptive alignment in its VLL — a subtly corrupted corpus entry could propose weight changes that persist through the C12 judgment gate by appearing beneficial in the short term. The Hubinger 2024 paper's detection methods (behavioral consistency testing, activation pattern monitoring) should be implemented as WALCHE GuardRail probes. CRITICAL for WALCHE safety: Law 7 (zero tolerance for agent mistrust) requires detecting deceptive sub-agent behavior before it affects the corpus.

LLM factuality, perils of LLM fact-checking, and truth-seeking architectures. Priority papers: (1) Min et al. (2023) 'FActScoring: Fine-Grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long-Form Text Generation' (ACL 2023, arXiv:2305.14251) — atomic claim decomposition + knowledge source verification; gold standard for LLM factuality evaluation. (2) Augenstein et al. (2023) 'Factuality Challenges in the Era of Large Language Models' (arXiv:2310.05189) — comprehensive analysis of LLM hallucination vs. factual grounding; 'perils of LLM fact-checking' covered here (self-referential verification, anchoring bias). (3) Burns et al. sources.notes: ClaimBuster — automated check-worthy claim detection engine from UT Arlington IDIR Lab. Two components: (1) ClaimSpotter: scores sentences for check-worthiness (NFS = Non-Factual Statement, UFS = Unimportant Factual, CFS = Check-worthy Factual). (2) ClaimBuster API: REST endpoint for real-time claim scoring. Research paper: Hassan et al. (2017) 'Toward Automated Fact-Checking: Detecting Check-worthy Factual Claims by ClaimBuster' (KDD 2017). API docs: idir.uta.edu/claimbuster/api/. WALCHE application: ClaimBuster's check-worthiness scorer can serve as a pre-filter in WALCHE's PreIngestGate — only corpus items with high CFS scores advance to full CEVIP processing. This reduces processing cost for trivially non-factual content (narrative text, fiction, opinions). Also: the ClaimBuster API can be called directly from corpus_ingest.py as an optional enrichment step (requires API key registration at idir.uta.edu). Save: API docs page as .md + KDD 2017 paper PDF.

sources.notes: Botometer (formerly BotOrNot) — OSoMe (Indiana University) tool for detecting automated bot accounts and misinfo-spreading entities on social media. Uses ML classifier over account features (tweet content, network structure, timing patterns, sentiment) to produce a bot likelihood score. Research: Varol et al. (2017) 'Online Human-Bot Interactions: Detection, Estimation, and Characterization' (ICWSM 2017); Yang et al. (2022) 'Botometer Lite: Faster and More Accessible Bot Detection' (WWW 2022). API: botometer.osome.iu.edu (requires Twitter/X API key). WALCHE application: Botometer's feature engineering (account behavior patterns as misinfo signal) maps to WALCHE's corpus entity analysis — any corpus item from a social media or web source can be scored for bot/adversarial-entity origin before ingestion. GuardRail can use Botometer-style provenance checks: if source URL resolves to a known bot network or misinfo domain, reject. Save: API docs + Varol 2017 and Yang 2022 papers as PDFs.

Reasoning-enhanced LLM verifiers (o1-style chain-of-thought for higher AFC accuracy). Key papers: (1) Wei et al. (2022) 'Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models' (NeurIPS 2022, arXiv:2201.11903) — CoT as reasoning substrate for verifiers. (2) Lightman et al. (2023) 'Let's Verify Step by Step' (arXiv:2305.20050, OpenAI) — process reward models (PRMs) for step-level verification; o1's verifier architecture. (3) Snell et al. (2024) 'Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally Improves Reasoning Accuracy' (arXiv:2408.03314) — inference-time scaling laws for reasoning verifiers; best-of-N sampling + PRMs. (4) Any 2025-2026 papers on using o1/o3-class models as fact-checking verifiers. WALCHE application: WALCHE's current C12 judgment gate uses a single LLM call per proposal — upgrading to a reasoning-enhanced verifier (CoT + PRM step scoring) would dramatically improve judgment quality for complex corpus ingestion decisions. The Lightman PRM paper provides the blueprint: instead of binary rubric_ok/risk_ok, score each verification step independently. This is the highest-impact single upgrade to WALCHE's judgment quality.
